title: The resurrection body (1 Corinthians 15:35–44)
hook: sown a seed, raised a plant: perishable to imperishable
tomorrow: O death, where is your sting? (1 Corinthians 15:55)

segments.voice: Yesterday, praying for the dead: some Christians keep praying, others entrust. Your line was rest in peace. Did you read those letters as a request? Day one thousand three hundred twenty-five.

"How are the dead raised up? and with what body do they come?" That's not a skeptic's heckle from today. It's a question Paul puts in the mouth of "some man" in a letter to the church in Corinth. And it's a good question. If a body is buried and returns to dust, what exactly comes back? The same knees? The same scar? A body at eighty, or at twenty? People in Corinth seem to have found the whole idea hard to picture. Paul's reply starts bluntly, "Thou fool," but he doesn't leave it there. He answers with something you could hold in your palm: a seed. That seed carries today's word.

First, the seed. Paul says, in the King James words, "that which thou sowest is not quickened, except it die." And then: "thou sowest not that body that shall be, but bare grain." You don't plant a wheat stalk. You plant a small dry kernel, and what comes up looks nothing like it. Yet it's the same life. Something goes into the ground, and something rises, and they belong to each other. Second, God is good at bodies. Paul points around him: people, animals, birds and fish all have different flesh. The sun, the moon and the stars each have their own glory, and "one star differeth from another star in glory." The God who made that much variety, he's saying, can make a new kind of body too. Third, the list. Read it slowly: "It is sown in corruption; it is raised in incorruption: It is sown in dishonour; it is raised in glory: it is sown in weakness; it is raised in power." Each line is a before and an after. Fourth, the surprising phrase: "It is sown a natural body; it is raised a spiritual body." Spiritual body is not a ghost, and not a body made of fog. Some readers take it to mean a body fully alive with God's Spirit, still a body, but no longer headed for the grave. The creed in the Book of Common Prayer doesn't say the soul floats on; it says "the Resurrection of the body." Christians hold a hope with the same shape as the seed: real continuity, real change.

Here's the practice: plant a seed, now or later today. If you have one handy, an apple pip, a bean, a seed from a packet, hold it in your palm. If not, picture one. Settle, and breathe. Look at how small and dry it is. Nothing about it looks like what it will become. Then think of one person you've lost, and set them beside the seed in your mind. If you pray, you can read Paul's line slowly: sown in weakness, raised in power. If you don't, simply hold the seed and wonder. The bell holds the time.
The resurrection body. Paul's picture of the body raised by God: sown like a seed, perishable, and raised imperishable, a spiritual body.
Your line: sown, raised. If you can, put a seed in some soil today, a pot, a cup, a corner of the yard, and let it remind you of Paul's answer. Day one thousand three hundred twenty-five.

howItsDone: Christians confess the resurrection of the body in the Apostles' and Nicene Creeds, and 1 Corinthians 15 is among the readings offered for funerals.

match.prompt: the resurrection body — tap the pairs.
pairs: with what body do they come?
alive with God's Spirit, not a ghost

myth: Paul refuses to answer the question about bodies
he calls the asker a fool, then answers anyway, with a seed and the stars.
Paul says what's sown and what's raised look the same
you sow bare grain, not the body that shall be. same life, new form.
one star differs from another star in glory
Paul's way of saying God already makes many kinds of bodies and glories.

fork.setup: you're Paul. someone in Corinth asks how the dead can possibly be raised, and with what body. how do you answer?
options: point to a seed: what you sow is not what comes up.
say only the soul lives on, so bodies don't matter.
fork.reveal: he answers with a seed. "thou sowest not that body that shall be, but bare grain." then the list: sown in weakness, raised in power.

original.note: Greek: a spiritual body, Paul's phrase in 1 Corinthians 15:44.

trapdoor: what you thought: in heaven, people become ghosts.
what it means: Paul hopes for a raised body, like a plant from a seed: the same life, changed past dying.
what a scholar hears: sōma pneumatikon, a spiritual body. many readers take it as a body animated by God's Spirit, not a body made of spirit.
recall: the first and last Greek letters
